approved_definition_context: Fin n is the finite set0,...,n-1. Matrix m n Real is an m-by-n real matrix. Matrix.transpose is ordinary real transpose, multiplication uses finite sums and scalar multiplication is entrywise;1 denotes the square identity and0 the zero matrix.

The local lets specify every angle, frame coefficient and diagonal weight literally. Fin d indices are zero-based. The row quantity is the sum of squared real coordinates, the square of its Euclidean norm, not the default supremum norm of a raw function type.

Natural q and d carry the displayed strict2q+1<d condition. Square root is the nonnegative real square root; cosine and pi have their ordinary real meanings. Universal quantification, finite sums, conjunction, equality, real inequality and local lets have their usual meanings.
